---
title: "Your structural MRI project handover"
---

A future student should be able to understand what you tried, reproduce the accepted parts, and recognise what remains unresolved. Use this checklist with the student-project template.

## Project record

- Research question and whether the analysis was exploratory or pre-specified.
- Dataset accession, frozen version, access conditions, study citation, and inclusion rules.
- Input manifest, approved storage location, and provenance.
- Environment, hardware, tool versions, commands, and parameters.
- Run ledger, failed jobs, QC decisions, exclusions, and participant-join audit.
- Measure dictionary, statistical plan, effect table, and uncertainty.
- New figures with captions and a regeneration record.
- Known limitations, unsuccessful approaches, and recommended next task.

## Publishable material

Review privacy, data-use terms, attribution, and permissions before including images, notebooks, or outputs. A public GitHub repository is not the right place for restricted clinical data. Keep private approval records in approved institutional storage.

## Completion decision

Record what was actually tested, by whom, and on which environment/version. Link the task issue and reviewed PR. A passing site build confirms that the documentation renders; it does not validate the MRI analysis.

## Earlier placement work

The [earlier student guide](https://neuroimaging-guide.netlify.app/results) provides an external example of a research presentation. Its figures and reported findings have not been transferred or independently reproduced here. Permission and validation should precede any later import.
